key_insight: Electrode lattice vibrations can tune adjacent BiFeO₃ nanocapacitors, shifting ferroelectric transition temperatures and inducing antiferroelectric-like switching at ambient conditions.
engineering_relevance: Interfacial phonon bias offers an additional design lever for ultrathin ferroelectric devices beyond epitaxial strain and electrostatic screening; photovoltaic performance is not evaluated.
method: Use first-principles-accurate machine-learned interatomic potentials and molecular dynamics.
Model symmetric BiFeO₃ nanocapacitors with metallic perovskite oxide electrodes.
Vary electrode octahedral-tilt orientation and amplitude while holding elastic and electric boundary conditions fixed.
evidence_signal: Simulations show changes in competing BiFeO₃ phase stability, transition temperature, and switching behavior, but the abstract provides no numerical effect sizes or experimental validation.
watch_item: Practical implementation requires independent control of electrode tilt landscapes without altering strain or electrostatic screening.
paper_title: Engineering ferroelectric nanocapacitors through interfacial phonon bias
